analysis.title: Central Bank Policy Tracker: October 2026
key_insights: Over the last three months, 91% of DM central banks (GDP-weighted) raised rates and none cut. In EMs, 13% cut and 20% raised.
The GS Global Financial Conditions Index tightened 22bp over three months, with DMs +23bp and EMs +21bp, driven mainly by lower equity prices and higher long-term rates.
Financial conditions tightened most in India (+97bp), Norway (+82bp) and South Korea (+61bp). They eased most in Mexico (-79bp), New Zealand (-40bp) and Romania (-30bp).
GS revised policy rate forecasts in 13 economies over the last 30 days, mostly upward.

GS raised end-2026 forecasts by 25bp in Japan (to 1.50%), Canada (to 2.50%) and Australia (to 4.85%). It raised the UK end-2027 forecast by 25bp to 4.00% and the New Zealand end-2027 forecast by 25bp to 3.25%.

GS also raised end-2026 and end-2027 forecasts in Egypt (+100bp both years), Ukraine (+50bp both), India (+25bp; end-2027 +50bp), Russia (+25bp both), and Taiwan (+12.5bp; end-2027 +37.5bp). It raised the Czech Republic and Kazakhstan end-2026 forecasts by 25bp and the Brazil end-2027 forecast by 50bp.
GS forecasts global policy rates broadly unchanged at 3.4% (GDP-weighted) over the next four quarters, rising through 2027Q1 and easing later in 2027.

DM central banks are expected to hike 16bp on average over the next four quarters: Sweden +75bp, Japan +50bp, UK +50bp, New Zealand +50bp, Euro Area +25bp, Canada +25bp, Australia +25bp. The US is forecast to see no net change (+25bp by 2026Q4, then -25bp by 2027Q3).
EM central banks are expected to cut 49bp on average, with 265bp of cuts in CEEMEA and 60bp in Latin America, offset by 11bp of hikes in EM Asia.
Relative to market pricing, GS end-2026 forecasts are balanced in DMs and dovish in EMs. They are below pricing in 30% of DMs and 60% of EMs, and above in 30% of DMs and 33% of EMs.
Relative to consensus, GS forecasts are balanced globally: below in 38% of economies and above in 44%.

The largest end-2026 gaps between GS and market pricing are Israel (-1.3pp), Hungary (-0.6pp), Poland (-0.5pp), South Korea (-0.5pp) and Colombia (+0.7pp). The US gap is +0.1pp, with GS at 4.1% against 4.1% consensus.

Central bank balance sheets as a share of GDP remain above 2019 levels in New Zealand (+9pp), Australia (+3pp), Canada (+1pp) and the US (+1pp). They are below 2019 levels in Switzerland (-16pp), Japan (-9pp) and Sweden (-5pp).

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has argued for a smaller Fed balance sheet. GS is skeptical the FOMC supports large reductions, though modest reductions from regulatory changes that lower reserve demand are possible.
ECB balance sheet runoff is at about €40bn/month after PEPP reinvestments ended in 2024. The ECB kept minimum required reserves at 1%.
The BoE MPC plans to reduce its £488bn gilt stock to zero by 2034, averaging £46bn/year, and halted active sales to the private sector. APF auctions are paused pending a decision by April 2027.
The BoC has ended QT and is gradually resuming asset purchases, starting with its term repo program on March 5.

risk_factors: Tighter financial conditions from lower equity prices and higher long-term rates, with India, Norway and South Korea tightening the most.
The GS forecast sits above market pricing in 30% of DMs and 33% of EMs, so pricing could move toward GS if its hike calls play out.
Balance sheet policy changes, including a possible Fed reduction under Chair Warsh and the BoE's gilt sales plan, could affect long-term rates.
